newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: ASC to study Wallis Report recommendations.
newsitem.headline: ASC to study Wallis Report recommendations.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Wednesday it would carefully study the Wallis Report recommendations for a new regulatory body to be set up called the Corporate and Financial Services Commission (CFSC).
The companies regulator said it was willing and able to take on more responsibility if the government wished it to do so.

The ASC said in a statement the role of the CSFC -- combining the ASC's current function and part of the Insurance and Superannuation Commission's function -- closely followed one of the models proposed by the ASC.
The new regulator would also be given certain consumer protection responsiblities.

ASC chairman Alan Cameron said in the statement he believed the ASC was clearly used as the basis for the new body, which would have a much greater consumer protection role than the ASC currently had.
"The ASC is ready, willing and able to take on the consumer protection role as described in the Wallis Report if the government wishes it to do so," Cameron said.
The ASC had an excellent record in consumer protection and had increased its focus in this area considerably during the past two years, he added.
"It must be noted that the government has not yet responded to the part of the Wallis Report which refers to the CFSC.
"Some changes may need legislation. This will take some time to happen."

Treasurer Peter Costello released the Wallis report earlier on Wednesday, and said the government had decided to abolish its policy banning mergers between Australia's big four major banks and two largest life offices after considering the report.

However, Costello said the government had decided not to allow mergers at this stage between the major four Australian banks -- National Australia Bank, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, Westpac Banking Corp, Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd.
Australia's two largest life offices are the Australia Mutual Provident Society (AMP) and National Mutual Holdings Ltd.
